name: 廣島牡蠣 みやまえ 離れ (Hiroshima Kaki Miyamae Hanare)

claims.text: Menu is built on oysters, white-grilled anago, small sardines and teppanyaki, which in Japanese cooking typically use wheat-based soy sauce and seasonings; no gluten-free preparation is documented.
This is a seafood and oyster izakaya with no documented vegan or plant-based dishes; cross-contact with fish and shellfish should be expected throughout the kitchen.

name: 広島牡蠣と鉄板焼き 一娯一笑 (Hiroshima Kaki to Teppanyaki Ichigo Ichie)

claims.text: Cooking is done on a shared teppan griddle, and Hiroshima-style okonomiyaki (wheat batter plus noodles) is cooked on the same surface as other dishes, making gluten cross-contact likely.
Grilled oysters are finished with butter-soy sauce or ponzu, and teppanyaki dishes use soy-based seasonings; standard Japanese soy sauce contains wheat.
The menu centers on oysters, sea urchin, conger eel, and Hiroshima beef cooked on a shared griddle with butter and soy seasonings; no plant-based or vegan options are documented.

name: 広島牡蠣処 大衆酒場バケツ 立町店 (Hiroshima Kakidokoro Taishu Sakaba Baketsu T)

claims.text: Fried oysters and oyster gratin are on the menu, indicating wheat (breading/flour) is used in the kitchen.
Standard Japanese seafood izakaya dishes here rely on conventional wheat-based soy sauce; no gluten-free soy sauce is documented.
The menu is almost entirely oysters and other seafood, so vegan diners face pervasive seafood contact with no documented plant-based options.

name: 廣島辛つけ麺 くじら屋 (Hiroshima Kara Tsukemen Kujiraya)

claims.text: Wheat noodles are the base of both the tsukemen and abura soba, so the kitchen handles wheat throughout; no gluten-free preparation is documented.
The broth uses a soy-style seasoning typical of Hiroshima tsukemen, which is normally wheat-based; no wheat-free tamari is mentioned.
The dipping broth itself is seafood-based (oyster and scallop), so it is not separable from animal ingredients.

name: ひろしま きんちゃい屋 (Hiroshima Kinchaiya)

claims.text: Okonomiyaki batter, noodles, and sauces are wheat-based and cooked on a shared teppan griddle alongside all other dishes, so heavy gluten cross-contact is inherent.
Hiroshima okonomiyaki uses wheat-containing okonomiyaki/soy-based sauces; no wheat-free sauce is documented.
Dishes are cooked on a single shared griddle with pork, seafood, and egg, so vegan separation is not feasible.

name: 広島らーめん たかひろ (Hiroshima Ramen Takahiro)

claims.text: The ramen is a Hiroshima-style shoyu (soy sauce) tonkotsu, and soy sauce in Japan is normally wheat-based; oden broth is also soy-seasoned.
Broth is pork-bone based with chashu pork; oyster ramen and oden include seafood, so animal products are integral throughout the kitchen.

name: 広島大衆居酒屋 十升 流川通り店 (Hiroshima Taishu Izakaya Tomasu Nagarekawa-d)

claims.text: Menu features multiple breaded deep-fried items (homemade gansu fish-paste fritters, lever katsu breaded liver, fried oysters, anago tempura) that share fryer oil, presenting wheat cross-contamination risk.
Dishes are seasoned with standard Japanese soy sauce and soy-based dressings (e.g., anago sashimi with wasabi-soy or ponzu), which are wheat-containing; no gluten-free tamari is mentioned.
A seafood- and meat-centric izakaya (oysters, conger eel, pork offal, liver, chicken, sashimi) using fish-based dashi and seasonings; no documented vegan dishes or separate preparation.

name: 広島つけ麺 ひこ 流川店 (Hiroshima Tsukemen Hiko Nagarekawa-ten)

claims.text: The dipping sauce is described as soy-based, and standard soy sauce contains wheat.
The dipping broth is built on seafood (魚介) stock alongside vegetables, so it is not suitable for vegans/vegetarians.
